title: University of Sussex and Universal Quantum Demonstrate Laser-Free Axial-Mode Entangling Gate on Doppler-Cooled Trapped Ions - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Experimental sequence for implementation of the gate.

Researchers from the University of Sussex (Sussex Centre for Quantum Technologies) and Universal Quantum have experimentally demonstrated a high-fidelity, all-electronic two-qubit entangling gate operating on the axial stretch mode of Doppler-cooled ytterbium-171 (171Yb+) ions without ground-state cooling. Detailed in a preprint on arXiv, the σz ⊗ σz geometric phase gate uses submerged current-carrying wires and global microwave pulses to achieve Bell-state fidelities well above fault-tolerant thresholds at a mean thermal occupation of n̄ = 50(5) phonons—approximately 2.5 times the Doppler cooling limit.

Use arrow keys when focused.All-Electronic Axial-Mode Gate Specifications & Sequence ComparisonGate Protocol / ParameterControl Sequence & TimingMeasured Fidelity & RobustnessBlackman-Ramped SequenceTwo 150 μs gradient pulses (300 μs total gate time, 10 μs ramps, ~35 T/m axial gradient at 506.88 kHz) separated by a microwave Hahn-echo π-pulse.100.0+0.0−0.4% Bell-state fidelity (parity contrast 1.003(7)); maintains >99% fidelity across ±0.18 kHz detuning error.AESE Modulated SequenceTwo 285 μs super-Gaussian amplitude and detuning-ramped pulses (570 μs total gate time) for adiabatic elimination of spin-motion entanglement.100.0+0.0−0.3% Bell-state fidelity (parity contrast 1.004(7)); widens >99% fidelity window ~4× to −0.68 to +0.80 kHz and cuts 1 kHz mode-noise sensitivity by 230×.Trap & Scaling Projection171Yb+ pair trapped 125 μm above a 54 K microfabricated surface Paul trap with buried wires (11 μm deep) under a 1 μm gold ground plane.Replacing the copper mount with a ceramic or silicon spacer to suppress eddy currents projects ~90 μs gates at >99.99% fidelity (75 μm ion height, 190 T/m).

To prevent stray oscillating electric fields from heating or ejecting the ions, the team fabricated the current-carrying wires 11 micrometers beneath the surface of the microchip beneath an embedded gold grounding layer. By driving the axial stretch mode (499.63 kHz) rather than a radial mode, the architecture preserves compatibility with mixed-species sympathetic cooling across ions of differing masses, eliminates time-consuming sideband cooling sequences, and relaxes shuttling waveform tolerances in modular quantum charge-coupled device (QCCD) processors.

Modeling of the chip mount further indicated that eddy currents in the underlying copper heat sink currently induce AC Zeeman shifts that cap the applied magnetic gradient; substituting a non-conductive ceramic mount or silicon spacer is projected to reduce those unwanted fields by two orders of magnitude and enable sub-100-microsecond gates exceeding 99.99% fidelity.
